stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist completed no continuing education in the first calendar year of her two-year renewal cycle. She plans to complete all 40 contact hours in the second calendar year, including 30 hours of home study. Why does this plan fail?

choices.text: Because contact hours may not be earned in the second year of a cycle.
Because home study may not be applied toward the requirement at all.
Because 40 contact hours exceed the annual maximum permitted.
Because a minimum of 20 contact hours is required in each calendar year and hours may not be carried over.
Because pharmacy law hours must be completed before any other subject area.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 4.03(4) requires a minimum of 20 contact hours in each calendar year of the two-year cycle, and 247 CMR 4.03(5) bars carrying hours from one calendar year to another. A year with zero hours therefore cannot be repaired later. The plan also breaches the 15-hour annual home-study cap in 247 CMR 4.03(4)(b).

choice_analysis.A: Hours may be earned in the second year; the problem is the empty first year.
choice_analysis.B: Home study is permitted up to 15 contact hours per calendar year.
choice_analysis.C: There is no annual maximum of 40; there is a daily maximum of eight.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the annual minimum plus the no-carry-over rule defeats the plan.
choice_analysis.E: No sequencing requirement applies among subject areas.

related_facts: A registrant may not earn more than eight contact hours of continuing education in a calendar day.
explanation.mpje_trap: The cycle total is not a single pot; the annual minimum and no-carry-over rule make an empty year unrecoverable.

reasoning_steps: Read the 40-hour cycle total together with the 20-hour annual minimum
Apply the bar on carrying hours between calendar years
Check the home-study proposal against the 15-hour annual cap
